brief.recommendation: The blocker has been idle for 51.4s. Checkout is at 28% success (87/120 failed) vs 95% SLO, with $13,340/min at risk. The business tolerates at most 60s of degraded checkout. Waiting 51.4s of blocker runtime approaches the 60s boundary, and the trade-off analysis (BIZ-4) confirms the cost of waiting exceeds the tolerated degradation. Terminating the blocker risks an unknown-cost interruption with no registry entry (BIZ-2), but waiting also risks exceeding the 60s tolerance window.

audit.report: The adhoc_reporting batch_worker session (pid 130530) became the root blocker for checkout sessions, remaining idle in transaction for 51.4 seconds while last issuing SELECT 1. This caused checkout success to drop to 28% (87/120 failed) against a 95% SLO, putting approximately $13,340/min at risk. The business tolerance for degraded checkout is 60 seconds; the blocker's runtime approached this boundary. After three negotiation rounds, the guardians could not agree: the Database Guardian favored waiting given the blocker's dormancy and lack of protected settlements, while the Continuity Guardian rejected each proposal due to the unknown cost of interrupting an unregistered workload and the approaching 60-second tolerance limit, ultimately escalating the case.
audit.root_cause: The batch_worker session for adhoc_reporting (pid 130530) entered an idle-in-transaction state, blocking checkout sessions and causing checkout success to decay to 28% against the 95% SLO.
lessons: Before proposing to terminate a blocker, verify the workload is registered in biz.workload_registry; adhoc_reporting had no entry, making the cost of interruption unknown and termination unsafe.
audit.negotiation_critique: The Database Guardian progressively built a case for waiting by accumulating evidence (no protected settlements, no active change calendar), while the Continuity Guardian rejected each proposal because the blocker's runtime combined with the observed checkout failure rate exceeded the 60-second business tolerance, leaving no margin for further delay.
follow_ups: Register adhoc_reporting in biz.workload_registry with owner and cost information to enable safe termination decisions in future incidents.
Add a runtime alarm that flags when a blocker exceeds 50 seconds of idle-in-transaction time for workloads without a registry entry.
Review the consult_owner policy for adhoc_reporting to confirm whether any dormant window could activate and block checkout.
Run a post-incident replay of the lock_graph at the 51.4s mark to verify the exact sessions blocked and confirm no protected settlements were missed.
